html:
Hassan al-Turabi was a Sudanese Islamist thinker and politician, the leader of the National Islamic Front and the mind behind the Islamist state of the 1990s.

Educated in law in London and Paris, he led the Sudanese branch of the Muslim Brotherhood tradition from the 1960s, and joined the government of Nimeiry as it imposed Islamic law. He planned the coup of 1989 that brought Omar al-Bashir to power.

In the 1990s he made Khartoum a meeting place for Islamist movements from across the world, and Osama bin Laden lived there until 1996. He broke with Bashir in 1999 and was jailed several times. His ideas on women's rights and reform were more liberal than many Islamists', but his state was harsh in Sudan.
